stem: An analytics team needs to move a one-time 40 TB historical export from an on-premises NFS share into Amazon S3 as fast as the network link allows, with no ongoing hybrid access needed afterward.

choices.text: Run an AWS DataSync task against the NFS share
Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway to present the share
Stream the files into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams record by record
Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the on-premises share directly

rationale: DataSync is built for a one-time, high-speed online transfer from an on-premises NFS share into S3, using a purpose-built protocol that can saturate the available link. An S3 File Gateway is designed to keep serving an NFS share on an ongoing basis with a local cache, which is more than a one-time transfer with no further hybrid access needs. Kinesis Data Streams ingests a continuous stream of small records with a 1 MB per-record limit, not a bulk export of large files. A Glue crawler scans a data source that is already reachable to catalog its schema; it does not transfer files across a network.
